assessments.reasoning: The name-resolution rule explicitly excludes type parameters from nonlocal rebinding. The annotation-scope passage identifies both the enclosing declaration and the inner scope in which the attempted rebinding occurs.

challenge.method: Compare declaring the enclosing type parameter nonlocal with reading it or targeting a nearer ordinary function-local of the same spelling.
challenge.results: The exclusion turns on the target binding and attempted rebinding. A read does not perform that operation, and a nearer ordinary local is a different target.

limitations: The claim does not concern references that merely read a type parameter or an ordinary function-local with the same spelling in a different context.
The scope concerns a nonlocal directive targeting an actual enclosing annotation-scope type parameter. A read of that parameter and a separate ordinary local are outside the prohibition.
